name: Non-text Content
summary: Every image, icon, chart or other non-text item needs a text alternative that serves the same purpose, unless it is purely decorative, a test, or sensory-only content.
how_to_test: Check each non-text item for an accurate text alternative; confirm decorative items are hidden from assistive technology (alt="" or CSS background).

name: Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded)
summary: Prerecorded audio-only needs a transcript. Prerecorded video-only needs a transcript or an audio track describing the visuals.
how_to_test: Find audio-only and silent video content and confirm a text or audio alternative exists.

name: Captions (Prerecorded)
summary: Prerecorded video with audio needs synchronized captions, unless the media is itself an alternative to text and is labeled as such.
how_to_test: Play each video with sound muted and confirm captions include speech and meaningful sounds.

name: Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded)
summary: Prerecorded video needs either audio description or a full text alternative so people who cannot see it get the visual information.
how_to_test: Check for an audio description track or a text transcript that covers visual-only content.

name: Captions (Live)
summary: Live video with audio, such as webinars and streams, needs real-time captions.
how_to_test: Join a live event and confirm captions are available and keep pace with the speaker.

name: Audio Description (Prerecorded)
summary: Prerecorded video needs an audio description track for visual information not conveyed in the soundtrack.
how_to_test: Play the video with eyes closed and confirm essential visuals are described.

name: Sign Language (Prerecorded)
summary: Prerecorded video with audio should include sign language interpretation.
how_to_test: Check for a sign language track or embedded interpreter.

name: Extended Audio Description (Prerecorded)
summary: When natural pauses are too short for audio description, the video should pause to allow extended description.
how_to_test: Verify the player can pause automatically to fit longer descriptions.

name: Media Alternative (Prerecorded)
summary: Prerecorded synchronized media and video-only content need a full text alternative covering both audio and visual information.
how_to_test: Confirm a complete text document is available for each video.

name: Audio-only (Live)
summary: Live audio-only content needs a text alternative such as live captions or a live transcript.
how_to_test: Check live audio broadcasts for a real-time text alternative.

name: Info and Relationships
summary: Structure and relationships shown visually, such as headings, lists, tables, form labels and groupings, must also be available in code so assistive technology can convey them.
how_to_test: Inspect the DOM for semantic headings, lists, tables, label associations and groupings; check that visual structure matches the code.

name: Meaningful Sequence
summary: When the order of content affects meaning, the reading order in the code must match the intended order.
how_to_test: Disable CSS or use a screen reader to read the page in DOM order and confirm it still makes sense.

name: Sensory Characteristics
summary: Instructions must not rely only on shape, color, size, position, or sound to identify something.
how_to_test: Read instructions such as 'click the green button' and confirm another identifier is also given.

name: Orientation
summary: Content must not be locked to portrait or landscape unless a specific orientation is essential.
how_to_test: Rotate the device or emulator and confirm content works in both orientations.

name: Identify Input Purpose
summary: Form fields collecting information about the user, such as name, email or address, must expose their purpose through the autocomplete attribute.
how_to_test: Check fields that collect personal data for a valid autocomplete token from the HTML spec.

name: Identify Purpose
summary: The purpose of interface components, icons and regions should be programmatically determinable.
how_to_test: Check that components expose their purpose via ARIA, landmarks or standard vocabularies.

name: Use of Color
summary: Color must not be the only way to convey information, indicate an action, prompt a response, or distinguish an element.
how_to_test: View the page in grayscale and confirm links, errors, and status indicators are still distinguishable.

name: Audio Control
summary: Audio that plays automatically for more than 3 seconds needs a way to pause, stop, or control its volume independently.
how_to_test: Load pages and confirm any auto-playing audio can be paused or muted.

name: Contrast (Minimum)
summary: Text needs a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 against its background, or 3:1 for large text (18pt or 14pt bold).
how_to_test: Measure foreground and background colors with a contrast checker, including hover and focus states and text over images.

name: Resize Text
summary: Text must be resizable up to 200% without assistive technology and without loss of content or function.
how_to_test: Zoom browser text to 200% and confirm nothing is cut off or overlaps.

name: Images of Text
summary: Use real text instead of images of text, except for logos or where a specific presentation is essential.
how_to_test: Search for images that contain readable text and replace them with styled text.

name: Contrast (Enhanced)
summary: Text needs a contrast ratio of at least 7:1, or 4.5:1 for large text.
how_to_test: Measure contrast against the stricter 7:1 and 4.5:1 thresholds.

name: Low or No Background Audio
summary: Speech-only recordings should have no background sound, or background sound at least 20 decibels quieter than the speech.
how_to_test: Listen to speech recordings for competing background audio.

name: Visual Presentation
summary: Blocks of text should allow users to choose colors, limit line width to 80 characters, avoid justified text, use adequate spacing, and resize to 200% without horizontal scrolling.
how_to_test: Check text blocks for line length, alignment, spacing, and customization options.

name: Images of Text (No Exception)
summary: Images of text are only allowed for pure decoration or where the specific presentation is essential, such as a logo.
how_to_test: Check that no informative text is delivered as an image.

name: Reflow
summary: Content must reflow into a single column at 320 CSS pixels wide (400% zoom at 1280 px) without two-dimensional scrolling, except for content like data tables, maps, and toolbars that need two dimensions.
how_to_test: Set the viewport to 320 px wide and confirm there is no horizontal scrolling for normal content.

name: Non-text Contrast
summary: Interface component boundaries, states, and meaningful graphics need at least 3:1 contrast against adjacent colors.
how_to_test: Measure borders of inputs and buttons, focus indicators, icons, and chart elements against their surroundings.

name: Text Spacing
summary: Content must remain readable and functional when users override line height to 1.5, paragraph spacing to 2x, letter spacing to 0.12 em, and word spacing to 0.16 em.
how_to_test: Apply a text spacing bookmarklet or user stylesheet and check for clipped or overlapping text.

name: Content on Hover or Focus
summary: Content that appears on hover or keyboard focus must be dismissible, hoverable, and persistent until dismissed or no longer relevant.
how_to_test: Trigger tooltips and popovers, then confirm Escape closes them, the pointer can move onto them, and they stay visible.

name: Keyboard
summary: All functionality must be operable with a keyboard alone, without requiring specific timings for individual keystrokes.
how_to_test: Unplug the mouse and use Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Space, and arrow keys to complete every task.

name: No Keyboard Trap
summary: If keyboard focus can move into a component, it must be possible to move it out using standard keys or with clearly explained instructions.
how_to_test: Tab through every widget, modal, and embedded player and confirm focus can always leave.

name: Keyboard (No Exception)
summary: All functionality must be operable by keyboard with no exceptions for path-dependent input.
how_to_test: Confirm even freehand-style interactions have a keyboard equivalent.

name: Character Key Shortcuts
summary: Single-character keyboard shortcuts must be able to be turned off, remapped, or only active when the relevant component has focus.
how_to_test: Find single-key shortcuts and confirm users can disable or remap them.

name: Timing Adjustable
summary: If content has a time limit, users must be able to turn it off, adjust it, or extend it, with some exceptions such as real-time events.
how_to_test: Identify session timeouts and timed actions and confirm a warning and an extension option exist.

name: Pause, Stop, Hide
summary: Moving, blinking, scrolling, or auto-updating content that starts automatically and lasts more than 5 seconds needs a pause, stop, or hide mechanism.
how_to_test: Find carousels, tickers, and animated backgrounds and confirm each has a control.

name: No Timing
summary: Timing must not be an essential part of the activity, except for non-interactive synchronized media and real-time events.
how_to_test: Check that no task depends on time limits.

name: Interruptions
summary: Users should be able to postpone or suppress interruptions, except emergencies.
how_to_test: Check for notifications and updates and confirm users can defer them.

name: Re-authenticating
summary: When a session expires, the user can continue after re-authenticating without losing data.
how_to_test: Let a session expire mid-task and confirm entered data is preserved after sign-in.

name: Timeouts
summary: Users must be warned about inactivity timeouts that could cause data loss, unless data is preserved for more than 20 hours.
how_to_test: Check for a timeout warning stating the duration of inactivity that triggers data loss.

name: Three Flashes or Below Threshold
summary: Nothing on a page flashes more than three times in any one second unless below the general and red flash thresholds.
how_to_test: Review animations and videos with a flash analysis tool such as PEAT.

name: Three Flashes
summary: Nothing on the page flashes more than three times in any one second, with no exceptions.
how_to_test: Confirm no content flashes more than three times per second.

name: Animation from Interactions
summary: Motion animation triggered by interaction can be disabled unless essential, which is commonly done through the prefers-reduced-motion media query.
how_to_test: Enable the reduced motion setting in the OS and confirm non-essential motion stops.

name: Bypass Blocks
summary: Provide a mechanism, such as a skip link, landmarks, or headings, to bypass blocks of content repeated across pages.
how_to_test: Press Tab on page load and confirm a skip link appears or landmarks allow jumping to the main content.

name: Page Titled
summary: Every page needs a descriptive title that identifies its topic or purpose.
how_to_test: Check the title element on each page for a unique, descriptive value.

name: Focus Order
summary: Keyboard focus must move through interactive elements in an order that preserves meaning and operability.
how_to_test: Tab through the page and confirm the sequence follows the visual and logical order.

name: Link Purpose (In Context)
summary: The purpose of each link must be clear from its text or from its surrounding context.
how_to_test: Read links out of context in a screen reader links list and flag vague text such as 'click here'.

name: Multiple Ways
summary: Provide more than one way to find a page within a set of pages, such as navigation, search, or a sitemap.
how_to_test: Confirm at least two of navigation, search, sitemap, or index are available.

name: Headings and Labels
summary: Headings and labels must describe the topic or purpose of the content or control.
how_to_test: Review headings and labels for clear, descriptive wording.

name: Focus Visible
summary: Any keyboard-operable control must have a visible focus indicator.
how_to_test: Tab through the page and confirm every focused element has a visible indicator.

name: Location
summary: Users should be able to tell where they are within a set of pages, for example through breadcrumbs.
how_to_test: Check for breadcrumbs or other location cues.

name: Link Purpose (Link Only)
summary: The purpose of each link should be clear from the link text alone.
how_to_test: Review each link in isolation for a self-explanatory label.

name: Section Headings
summary: Use headings to organize content into sections.
how_to_test: Confirm long content is divided with meaningful headings.

name: Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
summary: When a component receives keyboard focus, it must not be entirely hidden by author-created content such as sticky headers, cookie banners, or chat widgets.
how_to_test: Tab through the page with sticky elements active and confirm no focused control is completely covered.

name: Focus Not Obscured (Enhanced)
summary: When a component receives keyboard focus, no part of it may be hidden by author-created content.
how_to_test: Tab through the page and confirm no part of the focused control is covered.

name: Focus Appearance
summary: The focus indicator must be at least as large as a 2 CSS pixel perimeter of the control and have at least 3:1 contrast between focused and unfocused states.
how_to_test: Measure indicator area and contrast change between focused and unfocused states.

name: Pointer Gestures
summary: Functionality that uses multipoint or path-based gestures, such as pinch or swipe, must also work with a single-pointer alternative like a button.
how_to_test: Identify gesture-driven interactions and confirm a simple tap or click alternative exists.

name: Pointer Cancellation
summary: Actions triggered by a single pointer should fire on the up event, or be abortable, undoable, or reversible.
how_to_test: Press and hold a control, move off it, and release to confirm the action can be cancelled.

name: Label in Name
summary: For controls with visible text labels, the accessible name must contain that visible text so speech users can activate them by speaking it.
how_to_test: Compare visible label text with the accessible name computed by dev tools.

name: Motion Actuation
summary: Functions triggered by device or user motion, such as shaking, must also work through a standard control and can be disabled.
how_to_test: Find motion-triggered features and confirm a UI alternative and a way to disable motion exist.

name: Target Size (Enhanced)
summary: Pointer targets should be at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels, with a few exceptions.
how_to_test: Measure interactive target sizes against 44 by 44 pixels.

name: Concurrent Input Mechanisms
summary: Content must not restrict users to a single input type such as touch only or keyboard only.
how_to_test: Check that the site works with mouse, touch, keyboard, and voice input simultaneously.

name: Dragging Movements
summary: Any action that requires dragging must be achievable with a single pointer without dragging, such as with buttons or a menu.
how_to_test: Find drag-and-drop and slider interactions and confirm a click or tap alternative exists.

name: Target Size (Minimum)
summary: Pointer targets must be at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, or have enough spacing so a 24 pixel circle centered on each does not overlap another target, with exceptions for inline links and essential cases.
how_to_test: Measure target bounding boxes and spacing; flag targets smaller than 24 by 24 pixels that are too close to neighbors.

name: Language of Page
summary: The default human language of each page must be set in code with a valid lang attribute.
how_to_test: Check that the html element has a lang attribute that matches the page language.

name: Language of Parts
summary: Passages in a different language than the page must be marked up with their own lang attribute.
how_to_test: Find foreign-language phrases and confirm they have a lang attribute.

name: Unusual Words
summary: Provide a way to find definitions for idioms, jargon, and unusual words.
how_to_test: Check for a glossary or inline definitions.

name: Abbreviations
summary: Provide a way to find the expanded form or meaning of abbreviations.
how_to_test: Check that abbreviations have expansions available.

name: Reading Level
summary: Where text requires reading ability beyond lower secondary education, provide a simpler version or supplementary content.
how_to_test: Run a readability analysis and check for simplified summaries.

name: Pronunciation
summary: Provide a way to determine the pronunciation of words where meaning is ambiguous without it.
how_to_test: Check for pronunciation guidance on ambiguous words.

name: On Focus
summary: Receiving focus must not trigger an unexpected change of context, such as navigating away or opening a dialog.
how_to_test: Tab to each control and confirm focus alone does not trigger navigation or major changes.

name: On Input
summary: Changing a setting or entering data must not trigger an unexpected change of context unless the user was told in advance.
how_to_test: Change selects, radios, and checkboxes and confirm there is no automatic form submission or navigation.

name: Consistent Navigation
summary: Navigation mechanisms repeated across pages must appear in the same relative order each time.
how_to_test: Compare navigation across several pages for consistent order.

name: Consistent Identification
summary: Components with the same function across pages must be identified consistently, including their labels and text alternatives.
how_to_test: Compare labels and icons for the same function across pages.

name: Change on Request
summary: Changes of context should only happen on user request, or the user can turn them off.
how_to_test: Check that no context changes happen without explicit user action.

name: Consistent Help
summary: If a page offers help such as a contact method, chat, or FAQ link, it must appear in the same relative place on each page where it is offered.
how_to_test: Compare the position of help mechanisms across pages in the same set.

name: Error Identification
summary: When an input error is automatically detected, the item in error must be identified and the error described in text.
how_to_test: Submit invalid data and confirm each error is identified in text, not only by color.

name: Labels or Instructions
summary: Provide labels or instructions when content requires user input, including expected formats.
how_to_test: Check each field for a visible label and instructions on required format.

name: Error Suggestion
summary: When an error is detected and a correction is known, suggest the correction to the user, unless doing so would jeopardize security.
how_to_test: Submit invalid values and confirm error messages tell users how to fix them.

name: Error Prevention (Legal, Financial, Data)
summary: Submissions that create legal commitments, financial transactions, or change user data must be reversible, checked, or confirmed.
how_to_test: Complete these transactions and confirm users can review, correct, or cancel before finalizing.

name: Help
summary: Context-sensitive help should be available.
how_to_test: Check for contextual help on forms and complex tasks.

name: Error Prevention (All)
summary: All form submissions should be reversible, checked, or confirmed.
how_to_test: Check that every form submission allows review and correction.

name: Redundant Entry
summary: Information the user already entered in the same process must be auto-populated or selectable, rather than requiring re-entry, with exceptions such as security or essential re-entry.
how_to_test: Run multi-step processes and flag any field that asks again for data already supplied.

name: Accessible Authentication (Minimum)
summary: Authentication must not require a cognitive function test, such as remembering a password or solving a puzzle, unless an alternative or assistance such as paste support or a password manager is available.
how_to_test: Log in using a password manager and paste, and flag steps requiring transcription or puzzle solving.

name: Accessible Authentication (Enhanced)
summary: Authentication must not require a cognitive function test, with no exceptions for object recognition or personal content.
how_to_test: Confirm that no authentication step relies on a cognitive test.

name: Parsing
summary: Markup needs complete start and end tags, correct nesting, no duplicate attributes, and unique IDs. Removed in WCAG 2.2 because modern browsers and assistive technology recover from parsing errors, but it remains a Level A criterion in WCAG 2.0 and 2.1.
how_to_test: Validate markup for unclosed elements, duplicate IDs, and duplicate attributes. Not a conformance requirement under WCAG 2.2.

name: Name, Role, Value
summary: Every user interface component must expose its name and role in code, and state and value changes must be available to assistive technology.
how_to_test: Inspect the accessibility tree and verify name, role, state, and value for custom and native controls.

name: Status Messages
summary: Status messages such as search results, confirmations, and errors must be announced to assistive technology without moving focus, typically using ARIA live regions or role=status or role=alert.
how_to_test: Trigger status updates with a screen reader running and confirm they are announced without a focus change.
